intro: The second book of the Torah is called Shemot. That means "Names." Its English name is Exodus. It tells how Jacob's family became a people. It tells how they were slaves in Egypt. And it tells how they walked out free.

Jewish families tell this story every spring at Passover. Seven weeks later, at Shavuot, they remember a mountain. The Torah says the people heard ten sayings there. In this unit we learn what the Torah says. We learn what Jewish families do to remember. We do not decide if the story is true. We listen and we learn.
By the end, you will be able to tell the story of baby Moses and the burning bush. You will know why matzah is flat. You will know what the ten sayings are. And you will know what a mitzvah is.
bigQuestion: What does the Torah say about leaving Egypt and the mountain, and how do Jewish families remember it every year?

timeline.t: Jacob's family grows into a people in Egypt
A Pharaoh makes the people slaves
A mother hides baby Moses in a basket; Pharaoh's daughter finds him
The Torah says God speaks to Moses from a burning bush
Moses says, "Let my people go"; Pharaoh says no; ten plagues come
The people leave at night with flat bread, matzah; the first Passover
The sea opens; Miriam sings and dances
The people camp at Mount Sinai
Thunder and a cloud; the Torah says the ten sayings are given
Jewish families keep Passover and Shavuot every year

words.d: the English name for Shemot, the second book of the Torah; it means going out
a king of Egypt in the Torah's story
the baby in the basket, who grew up to lead the people out of Egypt
flat bread with no time to rise; Jewish families eat it at Passover
the Passover meal where Jewish families tell the Exodus story in order
the mountain where the Torah says the people heard the ten sayings
a commandment in the Torah; many Jewish people also use it to mean a good deed
the holiday seven weeks after Passover; Jewish tradition links it to the giving of the Torah

test.q: What is the English name for Shemot?
test.why: Shemot means "Names." Its English name is Exodus.

test.q: What does the Torah say Pharaoh did to the people?
test.why: The Torah says Pharaoh made the people slaves in Egypt.

test.q: Who does the Torah say found baby Moses in the basket?
test.why: Pharaoh's daughter found the basket. Miriam watched from far away.

test.q: What was strange about the bush Moses saw?
choices: It burned but did not burn up
test.why: The Torah says the bush burned with fire but was not burned up.

test.q: How many plagues does the Torah say came to Egypt?
test.why: The Torah tells of ten plagues, from the river turning red to darkness.

choices: It was baked in the sea
The bread had no time to rise
test.why: The Torah says the people left in a hurry, so the dough had no time to rise.

test.q: Who took a drum and sang after the sea opened?
test.why: The Torah says Miriam took a drum, and the women danced and sang with her.

test.q: What does Jewish tradition call the Ten Commandments?
test.why: Jewish tradition calls them the Ten Sayings. They were given at Mount Sinai.
A mitzvah is a commandment in the Torah. Many people also use it for a good deed.

test.q: Which holiday do Jewish families link to Mount Sinai?
test.why: Shavuot comes seven weeks after Passover. Jewish tradition links it to the giving of the Torah.

write.prompt: Draw or tell the story of one night: the night the people left Egypt, or the day at the mountain. Use the Torah's words from Exodus 12 (the flat bread) or Exodus 20 (the ten sayings). Say what the Torah says happened, and say one thing a Jewish family does today to remember it.
tips: Name the book: Exodus, also called Shemot.
Use two unit words, like matzah or mitzvah.
Tell what Jewish families do, not what you think everyone should believe.
